_about: Hand-maintained list of what the site tracks. Edit this file to add or remove races. Candidate 'fec' blocks tell scripts/fetch_fec.py how to find each candidate in the FEC database; add "fec_id" to pin an exact candidate if the search ever picks the wrong person.

sections.title: U.S. Senate: key races
sections.blurb: 35 seats are up. Republicans hold 53, Democrats 47 (including two independents who caucus with them). Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats for control.

sections.title: U.S. House: races to watch
sections.blurb: All 435 seats are up; 218 wins the majority. These ten were singled out by NewsNation as likely to decide control.

sections.title: Missouri
sections.blurb: Courts ruled the 2025 congressional map can't be used this year, so November uses the 2022 district lines. Most of Kansas City is in the 5th District; the Northland and Parkville (Platte County) are in the 6th.

races.title: U.S. House, MO 6th
races.note: Open seat (Sam Graves retiring); includes Parkville and the Northland

races.title: State Auditor
races.note: Only statewide office on the ballot

measures.title: Amendment 3
measures.yes: Repeals the 2024 reproductive-rights amendment; allows abortion only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, rape or incest; bans gender-transition procedures and puberty blockers for minors.
measures.no: Keeps the 2024 reproductive-rights amendment in the constitution.

measures.title: Amendment 6
measures.yes: Lawmakers would need 80% of both chambers, plus voter approval, to change a voter-passed initiative; makes the initiative process a fundamental right.
measures.no: The legislature can keep amending or repealing voter-passed laws by normal votes.

measures.title: Amendment 7
measures.yes: Creates a permanent state investment fund whose earnings would eventually be used to cut and eliminate state taxes.

measures.title: Amendment 8
measures.yes: Puts elected, four-year-term sheriffs in the constitution as each county's chief law enforcement officer, and limits their removal. St. Louis city, St. Louis County and St. Charles County are exempt.
measures.no: Current state law on sheriffs stays as-is.

measures.title: Proposition A
measures.yes: Approves the 2025 congressional map for future elections. It splits Kansas City along Troost Avenue.
measures.no: Rejects the 2025 map and keeps the 2022 district lines.

sections.title: Kansas City & Parkville
sections.blurb: Kansas City has no city questions this November. Jackson County voters (most of KC) have a county executive race and a sales tax renewal. Parkville voters decide three property tax propositions; each can pass or fail on its own.

races.title: Jackson County Executive
races.note: First open race for the seat in 20 years

measures.title: Jackson County COMBAT Question 1
measures.yes: Renews the quarter-cent anti-crime sales tax (first approved in 1989) for 10 more years, about $31M a year for the jail, prosecutors, courts, police drug units and community programs like addiction treatment.
measures.no: The tax ends; community-funded programs would start closing in April 2027.

measures.title: Parkville Proposition P
measures.yes: Raises the city property tax levy to fund police salaries, equipment and training.

measures.title: Parkville Proposition I
measures.yes: Raises the levy for road repaving, curbs and sidewalks.

measures.title: Parkville Proposition F
measures.yes: Raises the levy to repair and upgrade city buildings, including a roughly 45-year-old transportation building.

sections.footnote: If all three Parkville propositions pass, the city's levy rises about 47%, roughly $25/month on a $400,000 home (city estimate). New rates would start in 2027.

sections.title: Ballot measures in other states
sections.blurb: A selection of the higher-profile statewide questions. Names and numbers come from State Court Report's 2026 guide.

measures.title: Nevada reproductive rights amendment
measures.summary: Second and final required approval to protect abortion until fetal viability in the state constitution.

measures.title: Virginia Question 1
measures.summary: Adds a right to reproductive freedom to the state constitution.

measures.title: Virginia marriage amendment
measures.summary: Removes the constitution's same-sex marriage ban and affirms that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender or race.

measures.title: Virginia voting rights amendment
measures.summary: Restores voting rights to people with felony convictions when they are released from incarceration.

measures.title: Idaho Proposition 1
measures.summary: Creates statutory protection for reproductive freedom and privacy.

measures.title: Massachusetts Question 8
measures.summary: Would repeal legal recreational marijuana sales.

measures.title: Michigan Proposal 1
measures.summary: Asks whether to hold a state constitutional convention.

measures.title: Alaska ranked-choice repeal
measures.summary: Repeals ranked-choice voting and open primaries adopted in 2020.

measures.title: Colorado Amendment 86
measures.summary: Makes it harder to redraw congressional districts, starting with maps drawn in 2028.

measures.title: Maryland congressional districts amendment
measures.summary: Exempts congressional districts from the constitution's legislative-district requirements.

measures.title: Ohio Issue 3
measures.summary: Adds a photo ID requirement for voting to the state constitution.

measures.title: Utah Amendment B
measures.summary: Requires 60% approval for citizen initiatives on certain taxes.
